Three-week kidney and blood pressure review in the clinic, combined with nephrology consultation and kidney ultrasound on one trip
Video visit four weeks after the losartan increase and dapagliflozin start, with home vital signs and home blood tests
Same-day home sick visit for vomiting and diarrhea
Home visit for the three-month kidney and blood pressure review
Video visit for the six-month kidney review, with home vital signs and home blood tests

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Start losartan 50 mg daily and raise it to the maximum dose of 100 mg for A2 albuminuria; check potassium and creatinine 2 to 4 weeks after each start or increase, accepting a creatinine rise of up to 30 percent

If a second sample confirms a urine albumin-creatinine ratio of at least 200 mg/g, add an SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin 10 mg daily) after the nephrology review, and check potassium and creatinine 2 to 4 weeks later
Stop naproxen and avoid all NSAIDs; acetaminophen for headache; check kidney function before any iodinated contrast; adjust drug doses to eGFR
Nephrology consultation to confirm the cause of chronic kidney disease with albuminuria in a woman in her fifties and to advise on treatment and follow-up

Sick-day guidance: during vomiting, diarrhea, or poor fluid intake, pause losartan, dapagliflozin, and any other blood pressure medicine, drink fluids, call the clinic, and restart after 24 to 48 hours of normal eating and drinking

CMID kidney and blood pressure monitoring: blood pressure every visit with home readings; eGFR and urine albumin twice a year at G3a A2; a metabolic panel with each draw; calcium, phosphate, and PTH every 6 to 12 months; vitamin D at baseline; hemoglobin and KFRE yearly; one lipid panel and a statin; medication review every visit; vaccines reviewed yearly
Atorvastatin 20 mg daily; vitamin D3 1,000 units daily with recheck of 25-hydroxyvitamin D, calcium, phosphate, and PTH
Vaccines for chronic kidney disease: PCV20 now, a two-dose hepatitis B series, and yearly influenza and COVID-19 vaccines

Home-centered care: home visits and video visits with her own validated blood pressure cuff, scale, thermometer, and pulse oximeter; mobile phlebotomy; clinic trips only for tests that need them, with several tasks booked on one quiet early appointment
PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at baseline and yearly; her long-standing wish for solitude is respected and not treated as a disorder unless symptoms cause distress or impairment
Sodium below 2 g a day, a plant-rich diet, and at least 150 minutes a week of activity, such as garden work and walking
Systolic blood pressure below 120 mmHg (KDIGO), and at least below 130/80, without lightheadedness
118/74 mmHg on losartan 100 mg and amlodipine 5 mg
Urine albumin-creatinine ratio down by at least 30 percent from baseline on an ARB and an SGLT2 inhibitor
118 mg/g at three months and 96 mg/g at six months, from 240 mg/g
Stable kidney function, with no fall in eGFR of more than 20 percent after the expected early dip
eGFR 50 at the six-month review (54 at baseline); a temporary fall to 36 during gastroenteritis recovered
36 ng/mL on vitamin D3; PTH 61 pg/mL
Care delivered at home or by video wherever safe, with clinic trips limited to tests that need the clinic
Two clinic trips in the episode, each combining several tasks; all other visits at home or by video

list.item: At intake, independent in all activities of daily living; headaches and tiredness cut her writing mornings short on most days [S]
Writing full mornings again and free of regular headaches by the six-month review [S]
Alert, precise, and articulate; quiet voice; answers fully but briefly and prefers to add details in writing [S]
Mood "tired, not sad"; affect reactive with dry humor; no suicidal ideation; cognition intact [S]
